question:
A class studies how inverse sine and inverse cosine reduce an angle lying in the third quadrant. Let $\theta\in\left[\pi,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right]$, and define $P=\sin^{-1}(\sin\theta)$ and $Q=\cos^{-1}(\cos\theta)$. The principal-value ranges of inverse sine and inverse cosine are $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ and $[0,\pi]$, respectively. The students must replace $\theta$ with angles in these intervals while preserving its sine and cosine values. They then compare $P$ and $Q$ and test the resulting relations at $\theta=\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$.

(a) Express $P$ in terms of $\theta$.

(b) Express $Q$ in terms of $\theta$.

(c) Determine $P+Q$ in terms of $\theta$.

(d) Evaluate $P$ and $Q$ when $\theta=\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$.
explanation:
(a)
For $\theta\in\left[\pi,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right]$, the angle $\theta-2\pi$ lies in $\left[-\pi,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, which is not completely inside the inverse-sine principal range. Instead, using
$$\sin\theta=\sin(\pi-\theta)$$
and
$$-\frac{\pi}{2}\leq\pi-\theta\leq0$$
we obtain
$$P=\sin^{-1}(\sin\theta)=\pi-\theta$$

(b)
Using the periodicity and symmetry of cosine,
$$\cos\theta=\cos(2\pi-\theta)$$
For the given interval,
$$\frac{\pi}{2}\leq2\pi-\theta\leq\pi$$
which lies in the principal range of inverse cosine. Therefore,
$$Q=\cos^{-1}(\cos\theta)=2\pi-\theta$$

(c)
Using the obtained expressions,
$$P+Q=(\pi-\theta)+(2\pi-\theta)$$
$$P+Q=3\pi-2\theta$$

(d)
For $\theta=\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$,
$$P=\pi-\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\frac{\pi}{6}$$
and
$$Q=2\pi-\frac{7\pi}{6}=\frac{5\pi}{6}$$
Hence, $P=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $Q=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$.
